# Card accessibility issues

> Generated by accessibility-auditor. Resolve these issues before using this component in production.

## Clickable card is not keyboard-accessible

**File:** `card.component.ts` — `isClickable` input / `card.component.scss` — `.is-clickable` rule

**WCAG criterion:** 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)

**Problem:** When `isClickable="true"` is set, the component adds `cursor: pointer` and a hover shadow via CSS, but does not add `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, or any keyboard event handler. A non-native-interactive host element (e.g. `<div>`) styled as clickable is unreachable via keyboard and has no announced role.

**Recommendation:** The consumer must add `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"` on the host element, plus `(keydown.enter)` and `(keydown.space)` handlers that invoke the same action as the click. Alternatively, use a native `<button corp-card>` as the host element so interactive semantics and keyboard support are provided automatically.

---

## Selected state not communicated to assistive technologies

**File:** `card.component.ts` — `isSelected` input / `card.component.scss` — `.is-selected` rule

**WCAG criterion:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)

**Problem:** When `isSelected="true"`, the component applies a primary-color border via CSS. This visual change is not exposed via any ARIA state attribute, so screen readers cannot inform users that the card is selected.

**Recommendation:** The consumer must add the appropriate ARIA state on the host: `aria-selected="true"` when the card is used inside a `role="listbox"` or `role="grid"` context, or `aria-pressed="true"` when used as a standalone toggle. The component could also expose a computed `aria-selected` binding in `host: {}` derived from the `isSelected` input.

---

## Focusable card cannot actually receive keyboard focus

**File:** `card.component.ts` — `isFocusable` input / `card.component.scss` — `.is-focusable` rule

**WCAG criterion:** 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A)

**Problem:** When `isFocusable="true"`, the component applies `:focus` and `:focus-within` border styles but does not add `tabindex="0"` to the host. A non-native-interactive element without `tabindex` cannot receive keyboard focus, so the styles are never triggered by keyboard navigation and the card is inaccessible via Tab.

**Recommendation:** The consumer must add `tabindex="0"` on the host element when using `isFocusable`. The component could also set `tabindex` internally via `host: { '[tabindex]': 'isFocusable() ? 0 : null' }` to remove the burden from the consumer.

---

## Focus indicator may not meet minimum contrast and area requirements

**File:** `card.component.scss` — `.is-focusable:focus` and `.is-clickable` rules

**WCAG criterion:** 2.4.11 Focus Appearance (Level AA, WCAG 2.2)

**Problem:** The focus indicator relies solely on a change of `--card-border-color` to `--color-primary`. WCAG 2.4.11 requires the focus indicator to enclose the component, have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors, and have a minimum area of the perimeter × 2 CSS pixels. A 0.1 rem border color change may not satisfy the area and contrast requirements in all theme configurations.

**Recommendation:** Add an explicit `outline` or `box-shadow` focus ring on `:focus-visible` that clearly encloses the card and guarantees at least 3:1 contrast against both the card background and the surrounding page background. Use `:focus-visible` instead of `:focus` to avoid showing the ring on mouse click.
